# vendor/

Privately vendored copies of nice-plug and baseview, behind `[patch.crates-io]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Lane FK of P1b made patches 1 to 5, lane FK2 patches 6 to 9 and lane FK of FU1 patch 10; the fork lane owns this directory, and no other lane edits it (a lane that needs a change asks for it).

Why vendored and not a git fork: a public fork would expose the project's name, CI would depend on Codeberg being up, and `deny.toml` would need `allow-git`. Decision and measurements: `docs/adr/0001-plugin-shell.md` and `docs/adr/0002-ui-toolkit.md` (notes of 2026-10-19), research session `_local/sessions/2026-10-19-p1b-plugin-editor/`.

The directory is outside the cargo workspace (`exclude = ["vendor"]` in the root `Cargo.toml`), so `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` and `--workspace` never touch it.

## Crates

Each package is the unchanged content of its crates.io `.crate` file at the version `Cargo.lock` pins. The bytes were taken from cargo's registry cache; each file's sha256 is the checksum `Cargo.lock` records (and the crates.io index serves), so they are the files crates.io hands out. Every entry keeps its crates.io version, so the exact `=` pins in the root `Cargo.toml` still match.

`nice-plug-derive` 0.1.2 and every other dependency stay on crates.io, unpatched.

Why egui-baseview is here: nice-plug-egui depends on it, and the keyboard-focus patch edits it. A `[patch.crates-io]` entry replaces a crate everywhere in the graph, so baseview (under egui-baseview) is the vendored one too.

## Licences

- nice-plug, nice-plug-core, nice-plug-egui: ISC, Copyright (c) 2022-2024 Robbert van der Helm. The crates.io packages carry no licence file; `LICENSE` in each of the three directories (added in the commit after the pristine import, the only file besides this README and `check-pristine.sh` that is not in a package) is the text of the repository's `LICENSE` at the Codeberg tag `v0.4.2` (fetched 2026-10-19).
- baseview, egui-baseview: `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE`, unchanged from the packages.
- Patch lines carry the licence of the crate they edit, so a human could still send them upstream.
- Entries in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: the project distributes these crates (compiled in) with local changes, so the file records them with the changes.

## Lints

Cargo caps lints in registry dependencies (`--cap-lints allow`) but not in path dependencies, and `[patch.crates-io]` turns these five crates into path dependencies. CI builds with `CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny`, so any warning a vendored crate produces fails the build. Pristine nice-plug 0.4.2 already warns in release builds (`param_ptr` and `param_value` in `wrapper/state.rs` are used only inside a debug assertion), and a newer toolchain adds new warnings to every crate it compiles.

Each vendored `Cargo.toml` therefore ends with a `[lints.rust]` table that sets `warnings = "allow"` (the only edit to a manifest; `vendor/check-pristine.sh` shows it). nice-plug's table also declares `cfg(enth_rtsan)` (`unexpected_cfgs`, patch 10's RealtimeSanitizer instrumentation). That gives these crates what a crates.io dependency gets. The `[lints]` table is the per-crate form of an `#![allow(warnings, reason = "...")]`, and it needs no source edit. Hard errors a toolchain bump introduces are not covered: they need a patch.

When you edit vendored code, build once with the `warnings = "allow"` line removed from the crate you touched (keep nice-plug's `unexpected_cfgs` line), so that your own change is warning-free; then put the line back. Patch 10 was checked that way with `cargo clippy -p nice-plug` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and `aarch64-apple-darwin`: no warning.

## Patches

Everything here is one git commit per change, after a single pristine-import commit. `git log --oneline -- vendor` is the list, and `vendor/check-pristine.sh` (`--full` for the whole diff) compares the tree with the `.crate` files in cargo's registry cache and checks their sha256 against the table above.

| # | Crate | Change | Size | Upstream status (1–5: 2026-10-19; 6–9: 2026-10-20; 10: 2026-10-21) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | nice-plug, nice-plug-core | **Slot rename.** `Param::display_name()` / `set_display_name(Option<String>)` (a `Mutex<Option<String>>` override in every `ParamInfo`; main thread only) and `request_param_info_rescan()` on `ProcessContext` and `GuiContext`. CLAP then calls `clap_host_params.rescan(INFO \| TEXT)` on the main thread; VST3 calls `restartComponent(kParamTitlesChanged)`. The CLAP and VST3 parameter-info calls report the override. Add-only apart from four edited lines | 13 files, +123 / −4 | Not upstream (nice-plug `main` `7197104c0d`, 2026-10-18, has no runtime parameter names). From the Phase 0 spike (`scripts/nice-plug-0.4.2-rename.patch`, applied unchanged, zero fuzz). REAPER 7.82 shows CLAP renames within 50 ms and ignores the VST3 ones |
| 2 | nice-plug-egui | **`editor_closed()` is called.** nice-plug-egui 0.6.0 documents `NiceEguiApp::editor_closed()` ("Called when the editor is closed") and never calls it. `impl Drop for UserAppWrapper` drops the stored `egui::Context` and calls it when the baseview window is destroyed (on the GUI thread, once per `build()`) | 1 file, +9 | Not upstream (`main` `7197104c0d`). Document-versus-behaviour bug; the owner may report it as an issue in their own words |
| 3 | baseview | **xkb keymap leak.** `XkbcommonState::new` builds a keymap with `xkb_x11_keymap_new_from_device` and passes it to `xkb_x11_state_new_from_device`, which takes its own reference; the creator's reference was never released, so every editor open leaked one keymap (about 61 of the 77 KB per open/close cycle measured on spike-shell). The fix is one `xkb_keymap_unref(keymap)` after the state exists (`xkb_keymap_unref(NULL)` is a no-op) | 1 file, +4 / −1 | Not fixed upstream: baseview `master` `4c79df39b` (2026-10-09) still unrefs only the state; the leak came with PR #210 (2026-06-13); no issue found. The owner may report it, with the valgrind trace from Phase 0 lane H |
| 4 | baseview, egui-baseview | **Keyboard focus only while typing.** On X11 baseview never forwards a key it received, and egui-baseview took the input focus on every mouse press and kept it, so after one click on a knob the host's shortcuts (Space for play in REAPER) were swallowed; and because a child window that selects `KeyPress` gets the key even while the host's toplevel holds the focus, plain hovering already swallowed them. baseview: `WindowContext::set_keyboard_input(bool)` selects or deselects `KEY_PRESS` and `KEY_RELEASE` on the window (a window that does not select keys passes them to the host), and on enable takes the input focus and remembers the previous holder, on disable gives it back (previous holder, else the parent, else `PointerRoot`); `FocusIn` and `FocusOut` with pointer detail no longer count as keyboard focus. egui-baseview: `KeyboardFocus::{OnClick, WhileTyping}` (`EguiWindowSettings::keyboard_focus`, default `WhileTyping` for embedded windows; standalone windows keep `OnClick`). `WhileTyping` starts with keys deselected, takes the keyboard exactly while `Context::text_edit_focused()` after each frame, and ends the edit if another window takes the focus. The `focus().unwrap()` on click is gone. macOS and Windows: `set_keyboard_input(false)` does nothing and `true` is `focus()`; baseview 0.4.1 consumes every key there anyway, so the Windows editor still needs the owner's check | 8 files, +275 / −22 | Not upstream (checked 2026-10-19: baseview `master` `4c79df39b` selects `KEY_PRESS` on its window unconditionally and has no switch; egui-baseview `main` `1f645a35d2` is still the 0.9.0 commit and focuses on every click). Design choice, not a bug fix: the owner may propose it upstream. Tested under Xvfb with XTest (`vendor/tests/focus-probe/`): 11 of 11 checks in both a direct child and the reparented (CLAP) layout; negative control = the same probe with `on-click`, which shows Space swallowed on hover and the focus kept after a click. Not tested: REAPER on a real display (SWELL may reassign the X focus itself): owner check |
| 5 | nice-plug | **CLAP: a note-on ahead of a parameter change on the same frame is no longer lost.** With `SAMPLE_ACCURATE_AUTOMATION = true`, `handle_in_events_until` queued the events it met while it looked for the event that splits the buffer. A note, MIDI or polyphonic-modulation event on the splitting frame that the host listed *before* the splitting parameter or transport event was queued with a timing equal to the slice's length (one past its last frame); the plugin's `next_event` loop never reaches it, and the queue is cleared for the next slice. It now finds the splitting event first, and handles only the events before the first event of that frame, so all of the frame's events start the next slice at timing 0 in either order (VST3 already orders parameter changes before notes). Found by lane TH: `bursts --order notes-first` lost 337 of 346 notes at 1024 events on spike-shell | 1 file, +51 / −9 | Not upstream (`main` `7197104c0d`). Proof: `enth-test-host bursts --order both --capacity 1024` gives `applied_all_up_to_events` 4096 for both orders (before the patch: notes-first 64, params-first 4096), and identical peaks and `NOTE_END` counts in both orders at every count; negative control = the same command on the build without the patch (exit 1) |
| 6 | nice-plug, nice-plug-core | **Dirty marking.** nice-plug never told the host about a state change it cannot see, so REAPER kept the project clean after an editor-only patch edit (lane RH: `IsProjectDirty` 0 on CLAP and VST3). nice-plug-core: `context::host::{HostRequests, HostRequestsInner}`, a handle for requests made outside the activate, process and GUI contexts, and `Plugin::host_requests(&mut self, HostRequests)` (default: ignore it), which each wrapper calls once right after construction (after `editor()`, before any state load). `HostRequests::mark_dirty()`: CLAP `clap_host_state.mark_dirty()` (the wrapper now queries the host's `clap.state` at `init`), VST3 `IComponentHandler2::setDirty(true)` (a cast of the component handler). Both are main-thread calls: `schedule_gui` performs the task at once on the main thread and queues it otherwise (CLAP `request_callback`; VST3 the host's `IRunLoop` while the editor is open); a queued request absorbs later ones (a pending flag cleared before the host call), so a drag that edits every frame costs one host call per main-thread turn | 8 files, +198 / −5 | Not upstream (`main` `7197104c0d` has no `mark_dirty` or `setDirty`). Proof: `reaper-test --scenario dirty-flag`, `IsProjectDirty` 1 at once and 3 s after an editor-only edit on CLAP and VST3, and 0 with the editor open and nothing edited (`clean-without-an-edit`); negative control = the 15e197c bundle, 0 and 0 on both formats (exit 1) |
| 7 | nice-plug | **The VST3 MIDI CC parameters.** With `MidiConfig::MidiCCs` the VST3 wrapper maps all 130 MIDI controllers (CCs 0–127, channel pressure, pitch bend) on 16 channels to parameters through `IMidiMapping`: 2,080 parameters. They are flagged read-only and hidden (`kIsHidden`), but REAPER 7.82 lists every one (`TrackFX_GetNumParams` 2,155 for enth's 72; it reads them as not automatable, so it honours the flags otherwise). `Vst3Plugin::VST3_MIDI_CONTROLLERS: &'static [u8]`, default `ALL_VST3_MIDI_CONTROLLERS` (all 130): `getParameterCount` adds 16 per listed controller, `getParameterInfo` lists them channel by channel, `getMidiControllerAssignment` refuses the others. A controller's parameter id is unchanged (start + cc + channel × 130), so the process side is untouched. Debug assertions: entries below 130, none twice. `getParameterInfo` also refuses an index equal to the count (upstream checked `>`) | 3 files, +55 / −8 | Not upstream (`main` still maps all 130). Measured: enth maps CC 1 only, REAPER lists 91 parameters on VST3 (was 2,155; CLAP 75 either way); Steinberg's validator lists `MIDI Ch. 1 CC 1` … `MIDI Ch. 16 CC 1` and passes 47 of 47; `reaper-test --scenario mod-wheel` hears CC 1 on both formats |
| 8 | nice-plug, nice-plug-core | **A main-thread rescan request.** Patch 1 offered `request_param_info_rescan()` only on the process and GUI contexts, so a rename during a host state load (a persistent field's `set`, on the main thread) had to be requested from the next `process()`, where nice-plug's `schedule_gui` runs the task inline if the thread is the one it treats as main (a host may process on its main thread in an offline render): a host call from inside `process()`. `HostRequests::request_param_info_rescan()`: CLAP `rescan(INFO \| TEXT)`, VST3 `restartComponent(kParamTitlesChanged)` through a task of its own (a state load before the host set its component handler only warns in debug builds). From the state-load path it runs there and then, like nice-plug's own `rescan(VALUES)` after a load (`Task::StateChanged` from `set_state_inner`); from another thread it is queued. The wrappers' rescan request (also behind the two contexts) now coalesces like patch 6 | 5 files, +86 / −13 | Not upstream (no runtime names upstream). Proof: `vendor/tests/rename-check/run.sh` unchanged (one `rescan(INFO \| TEXT)` with the trigger, none without); `reaper-test` `param-renamed` passes on both formats; enth's in-process host asserts one request per load, made during the load, and that `process()` never asks |
| 9 | nice-plug | **No restart on a CLAP render-mode change, by choice.** On `clap_plugin_render.set()` while active, nice-plug calls `request_restart()` so that `Plugin::activate()` sees the new `ProcessMode`. REAPER calls `set(OFFLINE)` when an offline render starts and honours the restart about 30 ms of wall-clock time later, mid-render: a traced plugin was deactivated at engine frame 123,392 (2.57 s of a 4.1 s render) and a fresh engine continued the render, losing the note sounding there. The point depends on the render's speed, so every CLAP render differed (10 of 10), and under load the cut reached the notes `reaper-test` measures (the `clap/macro-automation` flake). VST3 renders were sample-identical (REAPER sets `kOffline` before activating). `ClapPlugin::CLAP_RESTART_ON_RENDER_MODE_CHANGE: bool`, default `true` (nice-plug's behaviour); `false` keeps the plugin active, and its next activation gets the new mode | 2 files, +15 / −1 | Not upstream (`main` restarts). Proof: traced, one activation and one continuous render with the patch; `reaper-test`'s `render-repeatable` (a second render of the same project is the same audio from 0.25 s on) passes on both formats in 5 of 5 full runs; negative control = the 15e197c bundle, CLAP fails it in 2 of 2 runs (differences from 3.595 s and 2.368 s) |
| 10 | nice-plug | **`is_main_thread()` never allocates.** In a host without CLAP's thread-check extension the CLAP wrapper answers `is_main_thread()` itself, and the VST3 wrapper always does (through the OS event loop); `schedule_gui()` asks it whenever `process()` schedules a GUI task: each parameter change (the editor is told), a voice-count change, a latency change. Upstream compared `std::thread::current().id()` under `permit_alloc` (a FIXME in `wrapper/clap/wrapper.rs`, `event_loop/linux.rs` and `event_loop/windows.rs`). On a thread where the plugin had not touched thread-local storage, the host's audio thread included, that allocated: glibc creates a `dlopen`ed library's TLS block for a thread on its first access (`__tls_get_addr` → `tls_get_addr_tail`, under `dl_load_tls_lock`, `malloc`; `elf/dl-tls.c`), and `thread::current()` builds a handle. A `thread_local!` of our own would allocate the same way (macOS creates a dylib's thread-locals lazily too). New `event_loop/os_thread.rs`: `OsThreadId` reads the identity the OS keeps in the thread's control block, with no TLS. Unix: `pthread_self()` and `pthread_equal()` (glibc: a load relative to the thread pointer, `%fs` or `tpidr_el0`, and `==`; `nptl/pthread_self.c`, `nptl/pthread_equal.c`, `sysdeps/{x86_64,aarch64}/nptl/tls.h`; Apple libpthread-539: TSD slot 0, `src/pthread_tsd.c`), through `libc` (Linux, BSDs) or declared against libSystem (macOS, where nice-plug has no `libc` dependency). Windows: `GetCurrentThreadId()`, declared against kernel32 (the `windows` crate's binding needs a feature nice-plug does not enable), the TEB's `ClientId` (Wine's `dlls/kernelbase/thread.c` reads it the same way). The CLAP fallback (`wrapper.rs` 394–406, saved at 806) and the Linux and Windows loops (`linux.rs` 60–64, `windows.rs` 178–182) compare it with the identity saved at construction; the macOS loop (`macos.rs` 117–122) calls `pthread_main_np()` instead of messaging `NSThread` (an `objc_msgSend` cache miss takes the runtime lock and may allocate). The one behaviour change: an OS identity can pass to a new thread after its thread exits (std's `ThreadId` never repeats); the saved one is the host's main thread. Under `--cfg enth_rtsan` only (nightly, `cargo xtask rtsan`), the CLAP `process` entry is a RealtimeSanitizer real-time context (`#[sanitize(realtime = "nonblocking")]`, `wrapper.rs` 2043, `lib.rs` 87), so the sanitizer sees the wrapper's own event handling, not only `Plugin::process`; no effect on other builds | 3 commits (fix, instrumentation, check-cfg): 8 files, +192 / −28 (`os_thread.rs` is 148 lines of it) | Not upstream (checked 2026-10-21: <https://codeberg.org/RustAudio/nice-plug> `main` `7197104c0d`, 2026-10-18, still has the three FIXMEs and the `NSThread` message; no issue or pull request found). The owner may propose it upstream. Proof: `cargo xtask rtsan`'s `no-thread-check` (a state load every 250 ms without thread-check: voice-count changes) and `no-thread-check-bursts` (parameter and note bursts without thread-check, a new audio thread per burst) are clean, and the other ten checks still pass (the control still caught); negative control = the same command on `5e394e4` (the instrumentation without the fix): both abort with exit 43, `malloc` ← `__tls_get_addr` ← `std::thread::current` ← `is_main_thread`, one through `Enth::process_block`, one through `Wrapper::handle_in_events_until` → `update_plain_value_by_hash`. Not tested: Windows and macOS (cross-target clippy only), VST3 under RTSan (the test host is CLAP only) |

## Tests

Everything here runs on a display only under Xvfb: the scripts unset `DISPLAY` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and start `xvfb-run` themselves, and the programs that open windows refuse to run on a display that Xvfb does not serve. Builds take the shared build lock (`flock -s /tmp/enth-quiet.lock`) and at most 3 jobs. Each directory under `vendor/tests/` is its own cargo workspace outside the root workspace, with its own `Cargo.lock`, and patches the five crates to this directory.

- `vendor/check-pristine.sh`: the import (sha256 of each `.crate`, and the diff against it).
- `vendor/tests/editor-cycles/run.sh` (patches 2 and 3, about 9 minutes with a warm cache): `enth-test-host editor-cycles` with 200 cycles on a copy of spike-shell that counts `editor_closed()` calls, built twice: against this directory and against stock crates.io (`fork/`, `stock/`). The fork must call `editor_closed()` once per `build()`, keep the anonymous PSS growth within 26 KB per cycle over the baseline without an editor, and keep the thread count constant; the stock build is the negative control (no calls, about 84 KB per cycle).
- `vendor/tests/rename-check/run.sh` (patch 1): a plugin built on the vendored nice-plug and a small clack host that processes on its own thread, services `request_callback` and reads `clap_plugin_params.get_info` before and after. With the trigger it must see the name change and one `rescan(INFO | TEXT)`; without it (control) neither. `enth-test-host`'s `rescan` handler does nothing, so it cannot show this.
- `vendor/tests/focus-probe/run.sh` (patch 4): a program that plays a host window holding the X input focus, embeds the egui editor in it as a child, and drives mouse and keyboard through XTest. `while-typing` (11 checks) and `on-click` (upstream's behaviour, the negative control: Space is swallowed on hover and the focus stays after a click), each as a direct child and reparented the way the CLAP wrapper does it.
- Patch 5 is measured with `enth-test-host bursts --order both --capacity 1024` on spike-shell (`tools/test-host/proof.sh` runs the control).
- Patch 10 is measured with `cargo xtask rtsan` (nightly; `docs/plugin.md`, "RealtimeSanitizer"): its `no-thread-check` and `no-thread-check-bursts` scenarios run the test host without CLAP's thread-check extension (the default; `ENTH_TEST_HOST_THREAD_CHECK=1` offers it) and must be clean. The negative control is the same command on the tree before the fix (`git revert --no-commit` of the fix commit): both abort with exit 43. `OsThreadId` has a unit test in `os_thread.rs` (the crate's tests do not run from the root workspace; it was run as a standalone `rustc --test` against the `libc` rlib: 1 passed).
- Patches 6 to 9 are measured in REAPER (`xvfb-run -a cargo xtask reaper-test --package enth-plugin`, `docs/plugin.md`): `dirty-flag` (6), `state`'s `param-count` and `midi-cc-params` and the `mod-wheel` scenario (7), `param-renamed` (8), `macro-automation`'s `render-repeatable` (9). Patch 8 also keeps `vendor/tests/rename-check/run.sh` passing. The unit side is in `crates/enth-plugin` (`lib.rs` and `tests_host.rs`: the dirty and rescan requests, the VST3 controller list against what the plugin reads).
